title: Asia and Africa, 500 to 1500
note: Between 500 and 1500, Tang and Song China led the world in technology and trade, the Mongols built the largest contiguous land empire in history, and gold and salt caravans across the Sahara enriched the West African empires of Ghana, Mali and Songhai, while Swahili ports traded across the Indian Ocean.

read.title: Connected worlds before 1500
text: Long before Europeans sailed around Africa, trade linked Asia and Africa in rich networks. China was the largest economy. Under the Tang and Song dynasties, Chinese officials were chosen by examinations on the Confucian classics, and inventors developed printing, the compass, gunpowder weapons and paper money.

In the 1200s the Mongols, united by Chinggis Khan, conquered lands from Korea to eastern Europe and sacked Baghdad in 1258. Their rule was violent, but the Pax Mongolica that followed made the overland routes safer, and merchants like Marco Polo crossed Eurasia. After the Mongols were expelled, the Ming dynasty sent Admiral Zheng He on great voyages across the Indian Ocean in the early 1400s, then turned inward.

In West Africa, camel caravans carried salt south across the Sahara and gold north. Control of this trade built the empires of Ghana, Mali and Songhai. Mali's ruler Mansa Musa became famous across the Mediterranean world after his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, and Timbuktu grew into a center of Islamic scholarship. On the east coast, Swahili city-states such as Kilwa traded gold and ivory with Arabia, India and China, and their culture blended Bantu and Arab traditions.

q.q: How did the Pax Mongolica affect trade?
o: It moved trade to the Sahara

q.q: What built the power of Ghana, Mali and Songhai?
